:::{#thm-precision-matrix-inverse}
#### The precision matrix is the inverse of the variance matrix

If $\vX$ has the [multivariate normal distribution](#def-mvn) $\Normal_p\paren{\vecf{\mean}, \matr{\covmat}}$,
then $\precision(\vX) = \inv{\matr{\covmat}}$.

:::

::: proof

Let $\matr{\Omega} = \inv{\matr{\covmat}}$.
Reordering the elements of $\vX$ reorders the rows and columns of $\matr{\covmat}$ and of $\matr{\Omega}$ in the same way,
so for each $i$ and $j$ we may take $X_i$ and $X_j$ to be the last two elements.

Cut $\matr{\covmat}$ into [blocks](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-diagonalization.html#def-block-matrix) with the first $p - 2$ elements in the first block.
By [the inverse of a positive definite block matrix](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-diagonalization.html#thm-block-inverse),
the last $2 \times 2$ block of $\matr{\Omega}$ is $\inv{\matr{S}}$,
where $\matr{S}$ is the [Schur complement](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-diagonalization.html#def-schur-complement) of the first block of $\matr{\covmat}$.
By @thm-mvn-conditional,
$\matr{S}$ is the [variance matrix](variance-covariance.qmd#def-cov-vec-x) of $\tp{(X_i, X_j)}$ given $\vX_{-ij} = \vx_{-ij}$,
so the [diagonal](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-matrices.html#def-diagonal-entry) elements $v_i$ and $v_j$ of $\matr{S}$ are the [conditional variances](variance-covariance.qmd#def-cond-variance) of $X_i$ and $X_j$,
and its off-diagonal element $c_{ij}$ is their [conditional covariance](variance-covariance.qmd#def-cond-cov).
The [inverse](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-matrix-inverse) of a $2 \times 2$ [matrix](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-matrices.html#def-matrix) gives the off-diagonal element of $\matr{\Omega}$:

$$
\ba
\matr{\Omega}_{ij}
&= \paren{\inv{\matr{S}}}_{12}
&& \text{(last block of } \matr{\Omega} \text{)} \\
&= \frac{-c_{ij}}{v_i v_j - c_{ij}^2}
&& \text{(inverse of a } 2 \times 2 \text{ matrix)}
\ea
$$

which is the [coprecision](#def-coprecision) of $X_i$ and $X_j$.

Taking $X_i$ alone as the last element,
the last $1 \times 1$ block of $\matr{\Omega}$ is $\inv{\matr{S}}$,
where by @thm-mvn-conditional $\matr{S}$ is the [conditional variance](variance-covariance.qmd#def-cond-variance) of $X_i$ given $\vX_{-i} = \vx_{-i}$.
So $\matr{\Omega}_{ii}$ is the inverse of that conditional variance,
which is the [conditional precision](#def-conditional-precision) of $X_i$.

:::
